transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?
Hi, Doctor. My sleep has been messed up for a long time, and no matter how I change my schedule I can’t seem to get any real rest. It's just really starting to catch up with me.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep even when you go to bed at a normal time, or is your main problem that your sleep schedule is shifted very late or very irregular?

My rotating shifts definitely make my schedule irregular, but the real issue is falling and staying asleep even when I'm in bed on time. I'll lie awake for over an hour with my mind racing about work quotas and homework, wake up several times during the night, and never feel actually rested.
When you are off work and free to sleep on your own schedule, do you still have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, or does your sleep improve a lot?

Even on my days off when I can sleep on my own schedule, it doesn't really get any better. I still lie awake with my mind racing about everything I have to do, and no matter how much I try to sleep in, I never wake up feeling rested or recharged.
How long has this sleep problem been happening, and has it been causing problems with your daytime functioning, like fatigue, poor concentration, or irritability?

This has been going on for a little over two years now, starting shortly after I took on my rotating-shift job alongside classes. The constant fatigue makes simple things like laundry or focusing in class feel exhausting, and it's gotten to the point where I'm turning in school assignments late, swapping work shifts, and skipping basketball practices with my friends.
When you are on vacation or have several days completely off from work and classes, do your sleep problems still happen the same way, or do they improve a lot?

Honestly, even when I have a few days off, the sleep problems don't really go away. My mind still races about all the things I need to catch up on, and I still wake up feeling just as exhausted. It's like I can never actually catch up on rest.
Do you ever have periods of at least 2 weeks when you feel depressed, lose interest in things you usually enjoy, or have thoughts of hopelessness or self-harm?

Yes, I've actually felt this low, heavy mood and lost interest in things I used to love, like basketball and dancing, for much longer than two weeks—it's been constant for over two years now. While I do feel really down and unmotivated, I don't have any thoughts of self-harm.

Have you ever had a stretch of at least 2 months when you felt back to your usual self with normal mood and interest, or has this low mood and loss of interest been present most of the time for the past 2 years?

No, I haven't had a break like that at all. This low, worn-down feeling has been there steadily for a little over two years now—about two years and four months—and it has basically just become my new normal. I haven't had any stretch during that time where I felt back to my usual self.
Have you ever had a separate episode in the past where you felt depressed or lost interest for at least 2 weeks, even after you had already been back to normal for 2 months or more?
No, I don't recall ever having any separate episodes of depression or losing interest in things before all of this started about two years ago. Before that, I was pretty much my usual upbeat self.
During this time, have you also had changes in appetite or weight, low energy, feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, or trouble concentrating most days?

Yes, I've lost my appetite and often skip meals or just pick at food, and I feel constantly exhausted to the point where even simple tasks take immense effort. My concentration is definitely affected too, because my mind is always racing with worries about school and work.
Have there ever been any periods of at least 2 months during the past 2 years when your mood and interest in things were back to normal, or has the low mood been present most days the entire time?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. This low, heavy feeling has been there steadily for the entire two years without any periods where my mood or interest went back to normal. It has just been a constant background heaviness that hasn't let up.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia): depressed/low mood and markedly reduced interest/pleasure have been present most of the day, more days than not, for over 2 years, with no symptom-free interval of 2 months or more. Associated symptoms include low energy/fatigue, poor concentration, and reduced appetite, with clear functional impairment in school, work, and social activities. Sleep disturbance is present but appears secondary to the chronic depressive syndrome rather than a primary sleep-wake disorder.
